title: Nick Kyrgios serves 1-month ban after testing positive for cocaine at ATP Tour event
content:
Nick Kyrgios can return to tennis after serving a one-month ban for a positive test for cocaine.

The 2022 Wimbledon finalist was provisionally suspended Aug. 4, and an investigation by tennis authorities found he ingested cocaine out of competition. The International Tennis Integrity Agency reduced Kyrgios’ ban from three months to one month after he agreed to enter a treatment facility.

When the suspension was made public, Kyrgios, 31, called his decision to take the drug at the Mallorca Championships, a grass-court event in Spain held in June, a “huge mistake.”

“I’m sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me. Above all, I’m sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets, and I’m deeply disappointed in myself.

“I’m not going to make excuses, but I do want to give some context about where I’ve been. The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally. My body hasn’t been able to do what my mind expects it to do, and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.”

Kyrgios, who lost his first match at the event to compatriot Adam Walton, will forfeit the rankings points and prize money he earned there, which amounted to just under $7,650.

Had the investigation found he had taken the drug in competition, he could have been banned for up to four years.

Kyrgios was previously critical of the outcomes in five-time Grand Slam champion Jannik Sinner’s and six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Świątek’s cases. Both players’ overall bans were reduced because of mitigating circumstances: Their positive tests for clostebol and trimetazidine, respectively, were deemed to be caused by contamination.

Kyrgios, who has played just four matches in 2026 as he navigates a late career defined by persistent and serious injuries, labeled the impact of the reduced bans “disgusting” for tennis.
